//: THE IK START IDENTITY GOLD STANDARD. The source of truth for the Identity Benchmarking page.
Transcribed from 'IK Start – Identity Gold Standard.pdf' (one page, no text layer -- it was
read as an image). Every 'name', 'eliteRange', 'bestAtIt', 'tagline' and footnote of the
club's ten markers is word for word from that page, in its order. Change them only when the
club changes the document.
Six of the club's markers cannot be measured from a StatsBomb match report. Each of those
is kept exactly as it was, under 'replaces.marker' of a substitute that stands in its place,
so all ten are still here in the document's order. To restore one, move it back out. The
substitutes are ours, not the club's:
* 'name', 'eliteRange', 'bestAtIt' -- of the measure the report does have.
* 'replaces.rationale' -- why that measure is the closest the report has.
* 'target.provisional' -- the range is not from the standard-setter clubs. It is derived
from Start's opponents in the match reports by
scripts/identity/derive_targets.py, and 'target.basis' says how. Replace
it when the club sets its own, and drop 'provisional' then.
What is NOT in the PDF, and is ours, for every marker:
* 'target'      -- the range as numbers, so a status can be worked out, plus the short
form shown in the Target column. The numbers must agree with 'eliteRange';
IdentityCatalogTests checks that they do.
* 'statusRules' -- the thresholds for Strong Alignment and Developing. Adjust them here.
* 'measurement' -- which value in the extracted match data answers the marker ('metric'),
or why nothing in a StatsBomb match report can ('notMeasuredReason').
A marker without a metric is shown as 'Not measured'. It is never
estimated, and never given another marker's number under its own name.
The match data itself is NOT in this file and not in git: see Data/Identity/Matches/README.md.
title: Gold Standard – The 10 Identity Markers
intro: Based on tactical analysis of our six professional standard-setter clubs — Barcelona, Bayern München, PSG, Como, Racing Santander & Malmö FF — these are the elite performance levels the IK Start academy aims for across our 10 identity markers.

why.title: Why these are the gold standards
why.text: Benchmarks combine consistent team averages (the floor of performance) with peak match data (the ceiling). For example, while Malmö FF usually maintain a high volume of progressive passes, their 112-pass match against Skövde AIK shows the absolute maximum vertical courage we want to encourage in our players.

substitutes.title: Substitute markers
substitutes.text: Six of the club's ten markers cannot be measured from a StatsBomb match report. Each has been replaced by the closest measure the report does have, and says which marker it replaces. Their ranges are provisional and do not come from the six standard-setter clubs: by the same method, the floor is the average of Start's opponents in the match reports and the ceiling their best single match.

//: Higher is better: above 'max' is Exceptional, from 'min' to 'max' is Elite Alignment, at or
above strongAlignmentAtFractionOfMin x min is Strong Alignment, at or above
developingAtFractionOfMin x min is Developing, anything lower is Below Target.
Lower is better (the club's PPDA) has its own absolute thresholds on the marker, under 'target'.

phases.title: In Possession
phases.tagline: The "Protagonist" — controlling the game's climate & vertical intent

target.basis: Start's opponents in 20 StatsBomb reports (U14, U15, U17; 1 Apr – 29 Aug 2026): their average, 67.5, up to their best single match, 140 by Stabæk U14 on 23 Aug 2026.

replaces.rationale: The report has no progressive-pass count. Open-play final-third passes are its closest measure of the same vertical intent.

measurement.notMeasuredReason: The StatsBomb match report has no progressive-pass count. Its passing tables split passes by final third, box and long balls, and none of those is a progressive pass.

target.basis: Start's opponents in 20 StatsBomb reports (U14, U15, U17; 1 Apr – 29 Aug 2026): their average, 470.9, up to their best single match, 596 by Rosenborg U17 on 7 Jun 2026.

replaces.rationale: Tempo is passes per minute, and the report has the passes but no playing time.

measurement.notMeasuredReason: The StatsBomb match report has no tempo figure, and no ball-in-play time to work one out from: its Possession % is each team's share of the passes, not of the time.

phases.title: Out of Possession
phases.tagline: The "Defending Forward" — aggression & tactical reading to suffocate opponents

target.basis: Start's opponents in 20 StatsBomb reports (U14, U15, U17; 1 Apr – 29 Aug 2026): their average, 181.7, up to their best single match, 298 by Haugesund U15 on 26 Apr 2026.

replaces.rationale: The report has no PPDA, but it counts the pressing itself: every time a player closes down an opponent on the ball.

measurement.notMeasuredReason: The StatsBomb match report has no PPDA. It counts pressures, which are a different measure, and gives no opponent passes or defensive actions by pitch zone to calculate PPDA from.

target.basis: Start's opponents in 20 StatsBomb reports (U14, U15, U17; 1 Apr – 29 Aug 2026): their average, 45.2, up to their best single match, 77 by Haugesund U15 on 26 Apr 2026.

replaces.rationale: The report has no regains by half of the pitch, but it counts the reflex behind a high regain: pressing within five seconds of losing the ball.

measurement.notMeasuredReason: The StatsBomb match report has no ball recoveries, and does not split any regain by half of the pitch.

target.basis: Start's opponents in 20 StatsBomb reports (U14, U15, U17; 1 Apr – 29 Aug 2026): their average, 63.5%, up to their best single match, 83% by Stabæk U14 on 23 Aug 2026.

replaces.rationale: The report cannot count every duel, but it has one in full: the defensive ground duel, tackles won out of attempted.

measurement.notMeasuredReason: The StatsBomb match report only gives tackles won out of tackles attempted, which are defensive ground duels. Aerial duels cannot be counted (Aer% is 0 both when a player had none and when they lost them all) and failed dribbles are not recorded, so a total cannot be calculated.

target.basis: Start's opponents in 20 StatsBomb reports (U14, U15, U17; 1 Apr – 29 Aug 2026): their average, 60.9, up to their best single match, 99 by Haugesund U15 on 26 Apr 2026.

replaces.rationale: The report counts only the regains that follow a pressure, so they have a range of their own, not Total Regains' 70 – 90.

measurement.notMeasuredReason: The StatsBomb match report only gives Pressure Regains: possession won back within five seconds of a pressure. That is part of a team's regains, not the total.

footnotes.text: lower = higher pressing intensity; 5.04 (Barcelona) is the elite ceiling for a suffocating high press.
identifies anticipation & football IQ ("Malmö style") rather than physical duels.
